summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -5 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates 0; dollar −; brl −; risk 0; energy −; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Rough rice +3.8%; weakest: KC wheat -12.3%. Key releases ahead: US Fed Chairman Warsh Speaks (11-16 12:00 PM ET); US Core Retail Sales m/m (11-17 8:30 AM ET); US Retail Sales m/m (11-17 8:30 AM ET); US FOMC Meeting Minutes (11-18 2:00 PM ET).

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 5.15% (-4 bp in a month), 2-year 4.88% (+6 bp); 2s10s curve +27 bp (-10 bp in a month). Yields are little changed on the month. T-bill yield 4.12% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 103.42 (+1.6% in a month, +5.2% YTD). A stronger dollar makes US grain, oilseeds, cotton and meat dearer abroad. USD/BRL 5.641 (+10.7% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.670 (-0.3%); USD/MXN 18.52 (+0.4%).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -2.0% in a month (+10.5% YTD); VIX 19.3. Neutral risk backdrop.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 88.25 $/bbl (-10.9% in a month), Brent 95.20, ULSD 4.281 $/gal (-9.4%), natural gas 3.16 (-6.7%). Lower crude weighs on soybean oil and corn through biofuel margins and on cotton via cheaper polyester.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -7.5% in a month, Shanghai Composite -3.5%, Hang Seng -2.8%, yuan +0.3% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 7 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (21%); S&P GSCI -7.4% in a month; gold -7.1%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
